currentContext.expansion: Expansion in the year was network- and platform-led rather than plant-led. Qualified Institutions Placement proceeds were earmarked across four heads - setting up and running operations of dark stores and warehouses, advertising/marketing/branding initiatives across business offerings, investment in technology infrastructure and capabilities including cloud infrastructure and software, and general corporate purposes. The dark stores and warehouses head was fully drawn down with no unutilized balance at the end of the period, while balances remain against the advertising/branding, technology infrastructure and general corporate purposes heads; amounts already paid from the current account during FY26 will be treated as utilized from the unutilized proceeds in the financial year ending March 31, 2027. In quick commerce the Company shifted to an inventory model, under which revenue now also includes the full monetary value of goods sold rather than only the marketplace commission. There was no change in the nature of business of the Company during the year. On the entity footprint, two wholly owned subsidiaries were incorporated - Blinkit Foods Limited on August 18, 2025 and Eternal General Service Foundation on December 18, 2025 - while overseas entities were rationalised: Zomato Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. was dissolved with effect from August 8, 2025, Zomato Internet Hizmetleri Ticaret Anonim Sirketi was liquidated with effect from December 9, 2025, Zomato Netherlands B.V. was dissolved with effect from January 27, 2026, and Zomato Media (Private) Limited in Sri Lanka was struck off with effect from April 2, 2026. As at March 31, 2026 the Company had sixteen direct subsidiaries and four step-down subsidiaries and no associate company or joint venture.

risks.note: Turnover rate for permanent employees was 54.02% in FY 2025-26 against 44.33% in FY 2024-25 and 37.00% in FY 2023-24, with female attrition at 65.30%. The Company attributes this to inter-company movements to subsidiaries, exits in frontline sales, customer support and logistics roles, and periodic realignment of workforce structure, roles and capability requirements - a persistent execution and knowledge-retention risk for a people- and technology-led platform.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration in a single business line
risks.note: On a standalone basis 93% of total turnover is contributed by the India Food Ordering and Delivery Business, with only the remaining 7% from other services, so standalone performance is heavily levered to one category.

risks.risk: Business-model shift to an inventory model in quick commerce
risks.note: Quick commerce moved to an inventory model under which revenue now also includes the full monetary value of goods sold and not just the marketplace commission. This structurally changes the asset and inventory base of the business and drove the scale-down of the non-restaurant part of the B2B supplies business.

risks.risk: Dependence on a delivery-partner ecosystem outside the reported workforce
risks.note: Delivery partners are classified as value chain partners and are explicitly not part of Eternal's workforce, and the Company engages no permanent workers. Last-mile capacity therefore rests on a contingent partner base whose ESG and labour disclosures were only voluntarily reported for the year.

On a standalone basis the Company operates only in India (35 locations across 28 states and 7 union territories) and the UAE, with exports at just 0.02% of standalone revenue from operations - limited geographic diversification against domestic demand or regulatory shocks.

risks.risk: Litigation and stakeholder-grievance exposure across multiple stakeholder groups
risks.note: Complaints tracked under the NGRBC principles include legal cases filed before courts of law by communities, by customers (end-users and restaurant partners) and by value chain partners (delivery partners and suppliers/vendors), alongside shareholder complaints filed on NSE and BSE and employee POSH, human rights, working conditions, health and safety and whistleblower complaints; some complaints remain pending resolution at year end, including carry-overs from FY25.

risks.risk: Limited boundary and estimation basis of environmental disclosures
risks.note: Energy, GHG, water and waste disclosures cover only directly leased offices under operational control and are apportioned and extrapolated based on data availability; employees also work out of 48 co-working spaces in India and the UAE whose electricity sits outside the operational-control boundary, creating measurement and future-restatement risk as value-chain reporting becomes mandatory.

The Company must keep adapting to the evolving BRSR framework under SEBI's January 30, 2026 master circular and subsequent guidelines, with reasonable assurance now required on BRSR core and select indicators - an expanding compliance and assurance burden.

one-line thesis: Two things changed this quarter, and both are structural. First, management **raised the Blinkit long-term steady-state margin from the 5–6% range to the 6% top end**, and paired it with a first-ever **GAAP EBIT margin target of 4%** — a shift from "we'll be profitable" to a specific, auditable unit-economics contract. Second, they **rewrote the store model**: capex per store **₹1cr → ₹2.5cr (+150%)**, NOV-per-store-per-day up only 60%, and net working capital guided down **18 → 14 → 12 days** — explicitly framing the whole thing as *"we are open with these numbers moving around... as long as the math on ROCE is stacking up well."* Meanwhile Q1 was called the **peak of competitive intensity to date**, and management's core claim is that discount-led rivals are in a trap they cannot exit. Blinkit grew **+21% QoQ in volume** with MTUs **>30mn**, on *fewer* store adds and *lower* marketing spend — the strongest evidence yet that the growth is not being bought.
financial scorecard (q1 fy27 — spoken it:
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | **not spoken on call** | — | In shareholder letter only; call started directly at Q&A |
| EBITDA / margin | **not spoken** | — | Consolidated EBIT margin confirmed **still negative** — *"given the margin of the business is negative, there's no ROCE"* |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | **not spoken** | — | — |
| Gross margin | not quantified | — | **Gross profit is net of all inventory losses** (~1.8% of NOV) — a disclosure convention worth carrying into models |
| Order book | n/a (platform) | — | — |
| Cash / net debt | not quantified | — | OCF flattered by a **one-off advance-tax refund** — explicitly *"nothing structural"* |
| Blinkit volume (orders) | — | **+21% QoQ** | Analyst-cited, management-confirmed; historical Q1→Q2 range 18–20% (26% last year) |
| Blinkit MTUs | **>30 mn** | sharp increase | Achieved on **lower marketing spend and fewer store adds** — mgmt says nothing was done differently |
| Blinkit NAOV | flat YoY, drifting down QoQ | 2nd straight QoQ decline | Attributed to intra-quarter pattern shifts + price-matching under competition |
| Stores added | **~200** | — | Against **~₹700cr capex** in the quarter (warehousing is lumpy) |
| Net working capital | **14 days** | from 18 days | Steady-state estimate now **12 days** |

> **Distortions to flag:** (i) OCF includes a **non-recurring tax refund** (over-paid advance tax on expenses of ambiguous allowability); (ii) **payables up ~₹1,650cr** — mgmt says purely scale-driven trade + expense payables, *"not necessarily trying to over-optimize on terms with brands"*; (iii) contribution margin lagged take-rate expansion because of **state minimum-wage hikes**, **summer last-mile costs** and **new larger stores in early ramp** — mgmt insists the correct comparison is YoY vs Q1 last year, not QoQ.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Blinkit steady-state margin RAISED:** long-term Adjusted EBITDA margin now guided to **~6% of NOV** (previously the 5–6% range) — *"we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier and hence, the communication."*
- **Blinkit GAAP EBIT margin: 4% long-term** — and management explicitly confirmed this is **after ESOP expense and depreciation**, i.e. a true GAAP number, not "adjusted."
- **Capex per store: ₹2.5cr** (up from ₹1cr; both comparable — both include warehousing). Actual realised capex/store over 6–9 months **expected to stay below ₹2.5cr** — *"you will find it is lower than INR 2.5 crore. We expect that to continue going forward."*
- **New-store throughput assumption: 2,100–2,200 orders per day per store** (up ~60% on the old model).
- **Net working capital: 12 days steady state** (currently 14).
- **NAOV: explicitly guided flat** — *"we don't think they should move up in a meaningful way"*; a Q3 seasonal uptick expected but no structural expansion.
- **Margin direction:** asked point-blank whether margins should keep improving with no near-term pressure, CFO answered *"At this point, we can say that."*
- **Competitor discounting expected to abate:** *"We expect this to not continue beyond the near future so we do think that this will come off."*
- **Bistro: ~10 kitchens added per quarter**, deliberately cautious until unit economics prove out.
- **Nugget: disclosure promised in "a couple more quarters."**
- **Inventory losses: ~1.8% of NOV, NOT expected to improve** — *"It has been fairly asymptotic so far. We don't expect it to be materially much better."*
- **Explicitly refused:** any Q2 growth guidance — *"we don't want to comment on the quarter right now, no guidance on that."*
- **Not mentioned this call:** the FY29 $1bn consolidated EBITDA target, the 60% QC CAGR, and the 3,000-dark-store-by-Mar-FY27 milestone — none reaffirmed, none withdrawn. **Track these.**
order book & pipeline: Not applicable. The forward pipeline is store/warehouse build: ~200 stores added in Q1, a deliberate move to **larger stores** (with existing stores being *upgraded* to larger properties where better real estate is available), plus **gourmet stores in tier-1 cities** to widen assortment. Management accepts some split orders as a consequence but is watching it — *"Customers value the availability of products more than split orders."*
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Blinkit (Quick Commerce):** +21% QoQ orders; MTUs >30mn; growth **overwhelmingly from existing cities**, not new geographies. Non-metros grow faster off a smaller base; competition concentrates in **groceries in top-tier cities**, causing some share shift there. Customer-spend Pareto is **much flatter than food delivery** (where top ~15–18% drive 80%) — a genuinely important structural difference.
- **Food delivery:** MTU adds *accelerating* in absolute terms for 3–4 quarters, from both new-user acquisition and higher frequency. Defending against **Toing and Ownly** via selective price competitiveness — notably the **Gold free-delivery threshold cut from ₹199 to ₹99**, which lowers cost for low-value orders. **Monthly active restaurant count dipped** — attributed to the **LPG situation** taking restaurants offline, not rationalisation.
- **District (Going-Out):** five categories; **dine-out and movies** are the largest; **retail stores and events** the most promising newer ones. Customer base is **smaller but higher-spending** (higher NAOV) than food delivery, and will be in **far fewer cities** than QC or food delivery. No growth trajectory offered — *"Difficult to say."*
- **Bistro:** ~10 kitchens/quarter; older kitchens showing throughput progress on assortment/menu-pricing/ops. **Separate entity, zero overlap in NOV or bottom line** with food delivery — stated twice, unambiguously.
- **Nugget:** an **enterprise AI product business**, still *"in a little bit of stealth mode."* Good traction claimed; **losses are largely manpower**, not GPU capex. More disclosure in a couple of quarters.
- **Hyperpure:** not discussed on this call.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Deeper price-sensitive cohorts unlocked **gradually** as scale-driven efficiency is passed through as permanent lower prices (not promotions) — the stated route to the *next* 30mn MTUs.
- **Gourmet / larger-format stores** widening assortment in tier-1.
- **Nugget** as an unpriced, undisclosed enterprise-AI option.
- Non-metro expansion accepted at **lower NOV/store** provided the 6% margin holds — *"if that NOV is still profitable at 6% margin, then that increases the top line for us."*
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **The trap argument (the central moat claim):** *"if you channel your supply towards providing discounts to customers, then that's what the business becomes... They will move to the next platform or the next platform, or they will drop out of the category. We don't see a recovery for platforms from this trap."* Management is claiming subsidy-acquired cohorts are **non-retainable by construction**.
- **Earned the hard way, not theorised:** *"Couple of years ago... we were the number three or four player, and our initial approach in those markets was like typical e-commerce thinking, that let's start discounting... That didn't work for us initially in some markets in the south. Eventually, what worked was working on the infrastructure growth... Now, we are the leading player by NOV in most of these markets."*
- **Structural reason discounting works less in QC than e-commerce — shelf space:** *"In quick commerce, you're working off smaller store sizes, so you have limited shelf space. Hence, if you are discounting in categories where the margins are low, then that's all that sells from that store."* A discount-led QC player cannibalises its own limited shelf into low-margin SKUs; an e-commerce player with warehouses does not. This is a **non-obvious, physical barrier** and the best-argued point on the call.
- **Retention as the scoreboard, not share:** *"the tracker is customer retention, which is better than what it has been. From our vantage point, therefore, if the market is expanding faster than us, it really doesn't matter to us."*
- **Cohort durability:** three-year-old cohorts spend **3x** what they did at acquisition — and crucially this is measured on the **full original cohort including churned users** (*"If you acquire 100 customers in the quarter... If 40 of them never show up again, then the retention is only 60%"*), so the 3x is not survivorship-flattered. Almost all of it is **frequency**, not basket size.
margins & cost dynamics:
- **Take rate rose but contribution margin did not follow.** Three named causes: (1) **state minimum-wage increases** implemented in multiple states; (2) **larger new stores** contributing at lower margins in early ramp; (3) **Q1 seasonality — higher last-mile cost in summer heat.** CFO's framing: judge contribution YoY vs Q1 last year, where *"a large part of gross profit increase or take rate increase has translated into contribution increase."*
- **NAOV structurally capped, by design:** two opposing drags — new assortment skews low-NAOV, and **higher frequency shrinks basket size** (*"as frequency of consumers increases on our platform, we see that they start ordering fewer items in a cart because it becomes a daily use case"*). Wallet share still rises; NAOV does not. Low-NAOV general-merchandise additions are **higher margin**, so mix doesn't hurt.
- **Inventory shrink ~1.8% of NOV**, perishables-driven, **netted inside gross profit (part of COGS)** — and treated as a floor, not an improvement lever.
- **Pricing philosophy:** *"Our baseline is usually what we think product prices can sustainably be in the long run... We usually don't discount for a shorter period of time just to get some customers."*
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **~₹700cr capex in Q1 against ~200 store adds** — nominally ₹3.5cr/store vs the ₹2.5cr guide. Explanation: **a large part of capex is warehousing, which is lumpy**; measured over 6–9 months, capex/store runs **below ₹2.5cr**. This is a **testable claim** — verify the trailing-4-quarter capex ÷ store adds next quarter.
- Capex/store up 150% while NOV/store/day up only 60%. Management does **not** treat this as dilutive: warehouse capex raises SKUs-per-warehouse and shipping efficiency across the network, so it is *"not only correlated to the store throughput."* The reconciling metric they offer is **ROCE, not margin** — *"The more we invest, even if the margins fall, as long as the ROCE remains high, the absolute dollar of profit on the business will be more."*
- Existing stores are being **relocated/upgraded to larger properties**, not merely added — a hidden, ongoing capex line.
capital allocation: The whole framework was restated as **ROCE-gated, with every other metric explicitly negotiable** — capex/store, NWC, NOV/store/day, EBITDA and EBIT margins can all move *"as long as the math on ROCE is stacking up well."* Candidly, **there is no ROCE today**: *"Right now, of course, the EBIT margin is negative. There is no ROCE. We are all talking about future here."* No buyback/dividend commentary. Working-capital release (18→14→12 days) is a real, unheralded source of self-funding.
risks & watch-items:
1. **The 4% GAAP EBIT / 6% adjusted EBITDA targets are long-term with no date attached** — and current consolidated EBIT is negative. Nothing to verify against for several quarters.
2. **Capex/store guide vs actuals gap (₹2.5cr vs ₹3.5cr realised in Q1)** — hinges on the "warehousing is lumpy" defence holding over a longer window.
3. **Competitive intensity called the peak "so far"** — a hedged claim, not a call that it has topped. If rival subsidies *don't* come off "beyond the near future," the price-matching drag on NAOV and contribution persists.
4. **Minimum-wage inflation is a recurring, policy-driven cost** with no pass-through lever named.
5. **Inventory shrink at 1.8% is admitted to be a floor** — no path to improvement.
6. **Silence on FY29 $1bn EBITDA / 60% QC CAGR / 3,000-store milestone.** Neither reaffirmed nor withdrawn; a quiet drop would be material.
7. **Nugget is an undisclosed, loss-making manpower-heavy investment** inside a company being valued on QC economics.
8. **Restaurant-count decline in food delivery** blamed on an external LPG disruption — verify it reverses next quarter rather than being structural supply churn.
9. **Refusal to guide Q2** removes the near-term verification anchor, notwithstanding the historical 18–20% Q1→Q2 pattern the analyst laid out.
10. **District trajectory explicitly unforecastable** by management's own admission.
management quality / tone: Unusually high-quality disclosure discipline: they **raised** a long-term margin target with a stated reason (higher capex/store buying efficiency and larger average store size), **volunteered** the GAAP-vs-adjusted distinction when pressed, **corrected** their own historical strategy error in public (the failed southern discount push), and **refused** to speculate on market share (*"We don't know, it's speculative"*) or to guide Q2. They also declined to dress up a tax refund as operating cash. The soft spots: no opening remarks at all (everything pushed to the letter), Nugget kept in stealth while consuming cost, and no acknowledgement of the FY29 targets set one quarter ago. Answers to weak questions were curt to the point of terse (*"Not really."*, *"Much flatter than that."*) — confident, not evasive.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The shelf-space argument is the real moat thesis**, not brand or scale: in QC, discounting *consumes the scarce asset* (shelf) rather than just margin. This does not apply to e-commerce and is the cleanest structural reason to expect discount-led QC entrants to fail.
- **MTUs jumped sharply on LOWER marketing spend and FEWER store adds** — and management, asked what they did differently, said *"Not really."* Either the category is pulling them along or retention compounding is now doing the acquisition work. Either way it decouples growth from spend.
- **The 3x cohort spend is on the *full* cohort including total churn** — a much stronger statistic than it first sounds, and the surviving-cohort number is "much higher."
- **Frequency growth mathematically suppresses NAOV.** Analysts modelling AOV expansion from assortment are working against the company's own daily-use-case dynamic.
- **Higher capex/store is a deliberate margin-for-ROCE trade** — smaller-city stores with lower NOV/day are acceptable *because* 6% still clears. This means future consolidated margin can drift **down** while the strategy is working exactly as intended.
- **Working capital is quietly becoming a funding source**: 18 → 14 → 12 days, driven by lower inventory days, *not* squeezing brand payment terms (which they explicitly said they are **not** optimising).
- Bistro's separate-entity structure means **reported food-delivery economics contain no own-kitchen subsidy** — relevant when comparing to peers who blend them.

one-line thesis: Two things changed this quarter, and both are structural. First, management **raised the Blinkit long-term steady-state margin from the 5–6% range to the 6% top end**, and paired it with a first-ever **GAAP EBIT margin target of 4%** — a shift from "we'll be profitable" to a specific, auditable unit-economics contract. Second, they **rewrote the store model**: capex per store **₹1cr → ₹2.5cr (+150%)**, NOV-per-store-per-day up only 60%, and net working capital guided down **18 → 14 → 12 days** — explicitly framing the whole thing as *"we are open with these numbers moving around... as long as the math on ROCE is stacking up well."* Meanwhile Q1 was called the **peak of competitive intensity to date**, and management's core claim is that discount-led rivals are in a trap they cannot exit. Blinkit grew **+21% QoQ in volume** with MTUs **>30mn**, on *fewer* store adds and *lower* marketing spend — the strongest evidence yet that the growth is not being bought.
financial scorecard (q1 fy27 — spoken it:
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | **not spoken on call** | — | In shareholder letter only; call started directly at Q&A |
| EBITDA / margin | **not spoken** | — | Consolidated EBIT margin confirmed **still negative** — *"given the margin of the business is negative, there's no ROCE"* |
| PAT (rptd & normalized) | **not spoken** | — | — |
| Gross margin | not quantified | — | **Gross profit is net of all inventory losses** (~1.8% of NOV) — a disclosure convention worth carrying into models |
| Order book | n/a (platform) | — | — |
| Cash / net debt | not quantified | — | OCF flattered by a **one-off advance-tax refund** — explicitly *"nothing structural"* |
| Blinkit volume (orders) | — | **+21% QoQ** | Analyst-cited, management-confirmed; historical Q1→Q2 range 18–20% (26% last year) |
| Blinkit MTUs | **>30 mn** | sharp increase | Achieved on **lower marketing spend and fewer store adds** — mgmt says nothing was done differently |
| Blinkit NAOV | flat YoY, drifting down QoQ | 2nd straight QoQ decline | Attributed to intra-quarter pattern shifts + price-matching under competition |
| Stores added | **~200** | — | Against **~₹700cr capex** in the quarter (warehousing is lumpy) |
| Net working capital | **14 days** | from 18 days | Steady-state estimate now **12 days** |

> **Distortions to flag:** (i) OCF includes a **non-recurring tax refund** (over-paid advance tax on expenses of ambiguous allowability); (ii) **payables up ~₹1,650cr** — mgmt says purely scale-driven trade + expense payables, *"not necessarily trying to over-optimize on terms with brands"*; (iii) contribution margin lagged take-rate expansion because of **state minimum-wage hikes**, **summer last-mile costs** and **new larger stores in early ramp** — mgmt insists the correct comparison is YoY vs Q1 last year, not QoQ.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Blinkit steady-state margin RAISED:** long-term Adjusted EBITDA margin now guided to **~6% of NOV** (previously the 5–6% range) — *"we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier and hence, the communication."*
- **Blinkit GAAP EBIT margin: 4% long-term** — and management explicitly confirmed this is **after ESOP expense and depreciation**, i.e. a true GAAP number, not "adjusted."
- **Capex per store: ₹2.5cr** (up from ₹1cr; both comparable — both include warehousing). Actual realised capex/store over 6–9 months **expected to stay below ₹2.5cr** — *"you will find it is lower than INR 2.5 crore. We expect that to continue going forward."*
- **New-store throughput assumption: 2,100–2,200 orders per day per store** (up ~60% on the old model).
- **Net working capital: 12 days steady state** (currently 14).
- **NAOV: explicitly guided flat** — *"we don't think they should move up in a meaningful way"*; a Q3 seasonal uptick expected but no structural expansion.
- **Margin direction:** asked point-blank whether margins should keep improving with no near-term pressure, CFO answered *"At this point, we can say that."*
- **Competitor discounting expected to abate:** *"We expect this to not continue beyond the near future so we do think that this will come off."*
- **Bistro: ~10 kitchens added per quarter**, deliberately cautious until unit economics prove out.
- **Nugget: disclosure promised in "a couple more quarters."**
- **Inventory losses: ~1.8% of NOV, NOT expected to improve** — *"It has been fairly asymptotic so far. We don't expect it to be materially much better."*
- **Explicitly refused:** any Q2 growth guidance — *"we don't want to comment on the quarter right now, no guidance on that."*
- **Not mentioned this call:** the FY29 $1bn consolidated EBITDA target, the 60% QC CAGR, and the 3,000-dark-store-by-Mar-FY27 milestone — none reaffirmed, none withdrawn. **Track these.**
order book & pipeline: Not applicable. The forward pipeline is store/warehouse build: ~200 stores added in Q1, a deliberate move to **larger stores** (with existing stores being *upgraded* to larger properties where better real estate is available), plus **gourmet stores in tier-1 cities** to widen assortment. Management accepts some split orders as a consequence but is watching it — *"Customers value the availability of products more than split orders."*
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Blinkit (Quick Commerce):** +21% QoQ orders; MTUs >30mn; growth **overwhelmingly from existing cities**, not new geographies. Non-metros grow faster off a smaller base; competition concentrates in **groceries in top-tier cities**, causing some share shift there. Customer-spend Pareto is **much flatter than food delivery** (where top ~15–18% drive 80%) — a genuinely important structural difference.
- **Food delivery:** MTU adds *accelerating* in absolute terms for 3–4 quarters, from both new-user acquisition and higher frequency. Defending against **Toing and Ownly** via selective price competitiveness — notably the **Gold free-delivery threshold cut from ₹199 to ₹99**, which lowers cost for low-value orders. **Monthly active restaurant count dipped** — attributed to the **LPG situation** taking restaurants offline, not rationalisation.
- **District (Going-Out):** five categories; **dine-out and movies** are the largest; **retail stores and events** the most promising newer ones. Customer base is **smaller but higher-spending** (higher NAOV) than food delivery, and will be in **far fewer cities** than QC or food delivery. No growth trajectory offered — *"Difficult to say."*
- **Bistro:** ~10 kitchens/quarter; older kitchens showing throughput progress on assortment/menu-pricing/ops. **Separate entity, zero overlap in NOV or bottom line** with food delivery — stated twice, unambiguously.
- **Nugget:** an **enterprise AI product business**, still *"in a little bit of stealth mode."* Good traction claimed; **losses are largely manpower**, not GPU capex. More disclosure in a couple of quarters.
- **Hyperpure:** not discussed on this call.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Deeper price-sensitive cohorts unlocked **gradually** as scale-driven efficiency is passed through as permanent lower prices (not promotions) — the stated route to the *next* 30mn MTUs.
- **Gourmet / larger-format stores** widening assortment in tier-1.
- **Nugget** as an unpriced, undisclosed enterprise-AI option.
- Non-metro expansion accepted at **lower NOV/store** provided the 6% margin holds — *"if that NOV is still profitable at 6% margin, then that increases the top line for us."*
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **The trap argument (the central moat claim):** *"if you channel your supply towards providing discounts to customers, then that's what the business becomes... They will move to the next platform or the next platform, or they will drop out of the category. We don't see a recovery for platforms from this trap."* Management is claiming subsidy-acquired cohorts are **non-retainable by construction**.
- **Earned the hard way, not theorised:** *"Couple of years ago... we were the number three or four player, and our initial approach in those markets was like typical e-commerce thinking, that let's start discounting... That didn't work for us initially in some markets in the south. Eventually, what worked was working on the infrastructure growth... Now, we are the leading player by NOV in most of these markets."*
- **Structural reason discounting works less in QC than e-commerce — shelf space:** *"In quick commerce, you're working off smaller store sizes, so you have limited shelf space. Hence, if you are discounting in categories where the margins are low, then that's all that sells from that store."* A discount-led QC player cannibalises its own limited shelf into low-margin SKUs; an e-commerce player with warehouses does not. This is a **non-obvious, physical barrier** and the best-argued point on the call.
- **Retention as the scoreboard, not share:** *"the tracker is customer retention, which is better than what it has been. From our vantage point, therefore, if the market is expanding faster than us, it really doesn't matter to us."*
- **Cohort durability:** three-year-old cohorts spend **3x** what they did at acquisition — and crucially this is measured on the **full original cohort including churned users** (*"If you acquire 100 customers in the quarter... If 40 of them never show up again, then the retention is only 60%"*), so the 3x is not survivorship-flattered. Almost all of it is **frequency**, not basket size.
margins & cost dynamics:
- **Take rate rose but contribution margin did not follow.** Three named causes: (1) **state minimum-wage increases** implemented in multiple states; (2) **larger new stores** contributing at lower margins in early ramp; (3) **Q1 seasonality — higher last-mile cost in summer heat.** CFO's framing: judge contribution YoY vs Q1 last year, where *"a large part of gross profit increase or take rate increase has translated into contribution increase."*
- **NAOV structurally capped, by design:** two opposing drags — new assortment skews low-NAOV, and **higher frequency shrinks basket size** (*"as frequency of consumers increases on our platform, we see that they start ordering fewer items in a cart because it becomes a daily use case"*). Wallet share still rises; NAOV does not. Low-NAOV general-merchandise additions are **higher margin**, so mix doesn't hurt.
- **Inventory shrink ~1.8% of NOV**, perishables-driven, **netted inside gross profit (part of COGS)** — and treated as a floor, not an improvement lever.
- **Pricing philosophy:** *"Our baseline is usually what we think product prices can sustainably be in the long run... We usually don't discount for a shorter period of time just to get some customers."*
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- **~₹700cr capex in Q1 against ~200 store adds** — nominally ₹3.5cr/store vs the ₹2.5cr guide. Explanation: **a large part of capex is warehousing, which is lumpy**; measured over 6–9 months, capex/store runs **below ₹2.5cr**. This is a **testable claim** — verify the trailing-4-quarter capex ÷ store adds next quarter.
- Capex/store up 150% while NOV/store/day up only 60%. Management does **not** treat this as dilutive: warehouse capex raises SKUs-per-warehouse and shipping efficiency across the network, so it is *"not only correlated to the store throughput."* The reconciling metric they offer is **ROCE, not margin** — *"The more we invest, even if the margins fall, as long as the ROCE remains high, the absolute dollar of profit on the business will be more."*
- Existing stores are being **relocated/upgraded to larger properties**, not merely added — a hidden, ongoing capex line.
capital allocation: The whole framework was restated as **ROCE-gated, with every other metric explicitly negotiable** — capex/store, NWC, NOV/store/day, EBITDA and EBIT margins can all move *"as long as the math on ROCE is stacking up well."* Candidly, **there is no ROCE today**: *"Right now, of course, the EBIT margin is negative. There is no ROCE. We are all talking about future here."* No buyback/dividend commentary. Working-capital release (18→14→12 days) is a real, unheralded source of self-funding.
risks & watch-items:
1. **The 4% GAAP EBIT / 6% adjusted EBITDA targets are long-term with no date attached** — and current consolidated EBIT is negative. Nothing to verify against for several quarters.
2. **Capex/store guide vs actuals gap (₹2.5cr vs ₹3.5cr realised in Q1)** — hinges on the "warehousing is lumpy" defence holding over a longer window.
3. **Competitive intensity called the peak "so far"** — a hedged claim, not a call that it has topped. If rival subsidies *don't* come off "beyond the near future," the price-matching drag on NAOV and contribution persists.
4. **Minimum-wage inflation is a recurring, policy-driven cost** with no pass-through lever named.
5. **Inventory shrink at 1.8% is admitted to be a floor** — no path to improvement.
6. **Silence on FY29 $1bn EBITDA / 60% QC CAGR / 3,000-store milestone.** Neither reaffirmed nor withdrawn; a quiet drop would be material.
7. **Nugget is an undisclosed, loss-making manpower-heavy investment** inside a company being valued on QC economics.
8. **Restaurant-count decline in food delivery** blamed on an external LPG disruption — verify it reverses next quarter rather than being structural supply churn.
9. **Refusal to guide Q2** removes the near-term verification anchor, notwithstanding the historical 18–20% Q1→Q2 pattern the analyst laid out.
10. **District trajectory explicitly unforecastable** by management's own admission.
management quality / tone: Unusually high-quality disclosure discipline: they **raised** a long-term margin target with a stated reason (higher capex/store buying efficiency and larger average store size), **volunteered** the GAAP-vs-adjusted distinction when pressed, **corrected** their own historical strategy error in public (the failed southern discount push), and **refused** to speculate on market share (*"We don't know, it's speculative"*) or to guide Q2. They also declined to dress up a tax refund as operating cash. The soft spots: no opening remarks at all (everything pushed to the letter), Nugget kept in stealth while consuming cost, and no acknowledgement of the FY29 targets set one quarter ago. Answers to weak questions were curt to the point of terse (*"Not really."*, *"Much flatter than that."*) — confident, not evasive.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The shelf-space argument is the real moat thesis**, not brand or scale: in QC, discounting *consumes the scarce asset* (shelf) rather than just margin. This does not apply to e-commerce and is the cleanest structural reason to expect discount-led QC entrants to fail.
- **MTUs jumped sharply on LOWER marketing spend and FEWER store adds** — and management, asked what they did differently, said *"Not really."* Either the category is pulling them along or retention compounding is now doing the acquisition work. Either way it decouples growth from spend.
- **The 3x cohort spend is on the *full* cohort including total churn** — a much stronger statistic than it first sounds, and the surviving-cohort number is "much higher."
- **Frequency growth mathematically suppresses NAOV.** Analysts modelling AOV expansion from assortment are working against the company's own daily-use-case dynamic.
- **Higher capex/store is a deliberate margin-for-ROCE trade** — smaller-city stores with lower NOV/day are acceptable *because* 6% still clears. This means future consolidated margin can drift **down** while the strategy is working exactly as intended.
- **Working capital is quietly becoming a funding source**: 18 → 14 → 12 days, driven by lower inventory days, *not* squeezing brand payment terms (which they explicitly said they are **not** optimising).
- Bistro's separate-entity structure means **reported food-delivery economics contain no own-kitchen subsidy** — relevant when comparing to peers who blend them.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
themes.driver: Blinkit dark-store rollout at the new INR 2.5cr/store capex against the 4% GAAP EBIT target; VMM small-format expansion; festive/quick-commerce GMV. Watch ARVINDFASN's SS27 sourcing lock (next 45-60 days) - if war-inflated input costs hold, apparel pricing corrects.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Eternal Limited (formerly Zomato Limited) is one of the first home-grown new-age tech companies listed in India, running four consumer and B2B internet businesses on a single platform base.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company operates through four key business segments: food delivery, quick commerce, going-out, and B2B supplies. Food delivery is a technology platform that lets customers search and discover restaurants, order food and have it delivered reliably and quickly, while quick commerce offers doorstep delivery of products across categories such as fresh, staples, electronics, beauty, general merchandise and festive needs. The going-out segment enables discovery of and transactions for dining-out, movies, sports and other live events and shopping, and the B2B supplies business supplies quality food ingredients and other products to restaurants.

margins.body:
- **Take rate rose but contribution margin did not follow.** Three named causes: (1) **state minimum-wage increases** implemented in multiple states; (2) **larger new stores** contributing at lower margins in early ramp; (3) **Q1 seasonality — higher last-mile cost in summer heat.** CFO's framing: judge contribution YoY vs Q1 last year, where *"a large part of gross profit increase or take rate increase has translated into contribution increase."*
- **NAOV structurally capped, by design:** two opposing drags — new assortment skews low-NAOV, and **higher frequency shrinks basket size** (*"as frequency of consumers increases on our platform, we see that they start ordering fewer items in a cart because it becomes a daily use case"*). Wallet share still rises; NAOV does not. Low-NAOV general-merchandise additions are **higher margin**, so mix doesn't hurt.
- **Inventory shrink ~1.8% of NOV**, perishables-driven, **netted inside gross profit (part of COGS)** — and treated as a floor, not an improvement lever.
- **Pricing philosophy:** *"Our baseline is usually what we think product prices can sustainably be in the long run... We usually don't discount for a shorter period of time just to get some customers."*

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: The whole framework was restated as **ROCE-gated, with every other metric explicitly negotiable** — capex/store, NWC, NOV/store/day, EBITDA and EBIT margins can all move *"as long as the math on ROCE is stacking up well."* Candidly, **there is no ROCE today**: *"Right now, of course, the EBIT margin is negative. There is no ROCE. We are all talking about future here."* No buyback/dividend commentary. Working-capital release (18→14→12 days) is a real, unheralded source of self-funding.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion in the year was network- and platform-led rather than plant-led. Qualified Institutions Placement proceeds were earmarked across four heads - setting up and running operations of dark stores and warehouses, advertising/marketing/branding initiatives across business offerings, investment in technology infrastructure and capabilities including cloud infrastructure and software, and general corporate purposes. The dark stores and warehouses head was fully drawn down with no unutilized balance at the end of the period, while balances remain against the advertising/branding, technology infrastructure and general corporate purposes heads; amounts already paid from the current account during FY26 will be treated as utilized from the unutilized proceeds in the financial year ending March 31, 2027. In quick commerce the Company shifted to an inventory model, under which revenue now also includes the full monetary value of goods sold rather than only the marketplace commission. There was no change in the nature of business of the Company during the year. On the entity footprint, two wholly owned subsidiaries were incorporated - Blinkit Foods Limited on August 18, 2025 and Eternal General Service Foundation on December 18, 2025 - while overseas entities were rationalised: Zomato Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. was dissolved with effect from August 8, 2025, Zomato Internet Hizmetleri Ticaret Anonim Sirketi was liquidated with effect from December 9, 2025, Zomato Netherlands B.V. was dissolved with effect from January 27, 2026, and Zomato Media (Private) Limited in Sri Lanka was struck off with effect from April 2, 2026. As at March 31, 2026 the Company had sixteen direct subsidiaries and four step-down subsidiaries and no associate company or joint venture.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Unusually high-quality disclosure discipline: they **raised** a long-term margin target with a stated reason (higher capex/store buying efficiency and larger average store size), **volunteered** the GAAP-vs-adjusted distinction when pressed, **corrected** their own historical strategy error in public (the failed southern discount push), and **refused** to speculate on market share (*"We don't know, it's speculative"*) or to guide Q2. They also declined to dress up a tax refund as operating cash. The soft spots: no opening remarks at all (everything pushed to the letter), Nugget kept in stealth while consuming cost, and no acknowledgement of the FY29 targets set one quarter ago. Answers to weak questions were curt to the point of terse (*"Not really."*, *"Much flatter than that."*) — confident, not evasive.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "No significant or material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals during the year impacting going-concern status or future operations, and there was no change in the Company's legal status. As at March 31, 2026 there was no application or proceeding pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; an earlier Section 9 petition by Nona Lifestyle Private Limited (Operational Creditor) was dismissed by the NCLT Delhi Bench II on November 25, 2024 and its restoration application was rejected on April 3, 2025. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the first home-grown new-age tech companies listed in India, giving early-mover positioning in Indian consumer internet
- Four complementary segments - food delivery, quick commerce, going-out and B2B supplies - spanning restaurant, retail and experience demand on one platform base
- Own dark store and warehouse network funded from Qualified Institutions Placement proceeds, supporting doorstep quick-commerce fulfilment
- Sustained investment in technology infrastructure and capabilities including cloud infrastructure and software

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **The 4% GAAP EBIT / 6% adjusted EBITDA targets are long-term with no date attached** — and current consolidated EBIT is negative. Nothing to verify against for several quarters.
2. **Capex/store guide vs actuals gap (₹2.5cr vs ₹3.5cr realised in Q1)** — hinges on the "warehousing is lumpy" defence holding over a longer window.
3. **Competitive intensity called the peak "so far"** — a hedged claim, not a call that it has topped. If rival subsidies *don't* come off "beyond the near future," the price-matching drag on NAOV and contribution persists.
4. **Minimum-wage inflation is a recurring, policy-driven cost** with no pass-through lever named.
5. **Inventory shrink at 1.8% is admitted to be a floor** — no path to improvement.
6. **Silence on FY29 $1bn EBITDA / 60% QC CAGR / 3,000-store milestone.** Neither reaffirmed nor withdrawn; a quiet drop would be material.
7. **Nugget is an undisclosed, loss-making manpower-heavy investment** inside a company being valued on QC economics.
8. **Restaurant-count decline in food delivery** blamed on an external LPG disruption — verify it reverses next quarter rather than being structural supply churn.
9. **Refusal to guide Q2** removes the near-term verification anchor, notwithstanding the historical 18–20% Q1→Q2 pattern the analyst laid out.
10. **District trajectory explicitly unforecastable** by management's own admission.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The shelf-space argument is the real moat thesis**, not brand or scale: in QC, discounting *consumes the scarce asset* (shelf) rather than just margin. This does not apply to e-commerce and is the cleanest structural reason to expect discount-led QC entrants to fail.
- **MTUs jumped sharply on LOWER marketing spend and FEWER store adds** — and management, asked what they did differently, said *"Not really."* Either the category is pulling them along or retention compounding is now doing the acquisition work. Either way it decouples growth from spend.
- **The 3x cohort spend is on the *full* cohort including total churn** — a much stronger statistic than it first sounds, and the surviving-cohort number is "much higher."
- **Frequency growth mathematically suppresses NAOV.** Analysts modelling AOV expansion from assortment are working against the company's own daily-use-case dynamic.
- **Higher capex/store is a deliberate margin-for-ROCE trade** — smaller-city stores with lower NOV/day are acceptable *because* 6% still clears. This means future consolidated margin can drift **down** while the strategy is working exactly as intended.
- **Working capital is quietly becoming a funding source**: 18 → 14 → 12 days, driven by lower inventory days, *not* squeezing brand payment terms (which they explicitly said they are **not** optimising).
- Bistro's separate-entity structure means **reported food-delivery economics contain no own-kitchen subsidy** — relevant when comparing to peers who blend them.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deploy Qualified Institutions Placement proceeds towards setting up and running operations of dark stores and warehouses, advertising/marketing/branding initiatives across business offerings, and investment in technology infrastructure and capabilities including cloud infrastructure and software
- Prepare sustainability disclosures under the evolving BRSR framework in line with the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct, with an external assurance provider appointed for core and select non-core KPIs
- Voluntarily extend ESG reporting to value chain partners ahead of the mandatory …

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (prior):** QC 60% CAGR through FY29; **$1bn consolidated EBITDA by FY29**; QC steady-state margin **5–6%**; **3,000 dark stores by Mar-FY27**; food delivery ~19–20% growth at ~5.5% margin; capex/store ₹1cr.
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** QC steady-state margin **raised to ~6%** (top of range) + **new 4% GAAP EBIT target** (incl. ESOP & depreciation). **Capex/store ₹1cr → ₹2.5cr**; NOV/store/day assumption +60%; **2,100–2,200 OPD/store**. NWC **18 → 14 days now, 12 steady-state**. ~200 stores added on ~₹700cr capex. Blinkit **+21% QoQ orders**, MTUs **>30mn** on lower marketing and fewer store adds; NAOV flat YoY, guided flat. Inventory losses **1.8% of NOV**, netted in gross profit, no improvement expected. Q1 declared **peak competitive intensity to date**; rival discounting expected to abate "beyond the near future." Bistro **~10 kitchens/qtr**, separate entity. **Nugget** (enterprise AI, stealth, manpower-led losses) disclosed as a segment for the first time — full disclosure promised in ~2 quarters. Consolidated **EBIT still negative → no ROCE**. Restaurant count dipped on the **LPG disruption**. Gold free-delivery threshold **₹199 → ₹99**. **FY29 $1bn / 60% CAGR / 3,000-store targets went unmentioned.**
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) trailing 6–9-month capex ÷ store adds actually below ₹2.5cr; (2) NWC moving 14 → 12 days; (3) Blinkit Q1→Q2 order growth vs the 18–20% historical band; (4) contribution margin catching up to take rate now that summer/minimum-wage effects lap; (5) whether competitor discounting in fact "came off"; (6) FY29 $1bn EBITDA and 3,000-store targets reaffirmed or quietly dropped; (7) Nugget disclosure delivered; (8) restaurant count recovering post-LPG; (9) Bistro kitchen adds ≈10._
